issues.headline: The November issue is here
issues.lede: Remembrance, bonfire night, life as a wartime evacuee in Shepley and the new Huddersfield Library.

articles.title: Welcome to November’s edition
articles.author: Shepley Magazine Team
articles.summary: From the Domesday Book to the planning boom: what new housing could mean for Shepley, a name for the Cask and Spindle, and bonfire night.
body: We know that Shepley is an ancient settlement, described in the Domesday Book in 1086 as “waste” after the Harrying of the North in 1069/70. By 1217 Shepley seems to have recovered, with the names of local landowners appearing in feudal records. The railway arrived in 1850 and Shepley boomed.

Planning applications for new developments have soared, not just in Shepley but throughout our local region – several hundred proposed new properties. New houses are needed, but is the destruction of ancient green land a positive or a negative thing? Please let us have your comments to our letters page.

The one village pub which could do with a new name is The Cask and Spindle (previously The Railway Hotel). How about The Shepley Lion, as the famed but mysterious beast was first reported from this pub’s car park in 2011?
Bonfire night at the cricket field is on November the 5th as usual. Please leave your car at home if you possibly can.

articles.title: Shepley Women’s Institute: Our clubs continue to keep busy
articles.author: Shepley WI
articles.summary: Fair Trade tea and coffee talk, the Strollers at Farnley Tyas, Gardening Group at the Health Centre and Crafts and Crumbs.
body: At a recent members’ meeting tea and coffee buyer Paul Jefferies taught us about sustainable tea and coffee farming and how Fair Trade organisations support young, female farmers.

The Strollers enjoyed a walk around the lanes at Farnley Tyas, finishing at The Golden Cock. The Gardening Group cut back the hedging shrubs at the entrance to Shepley Health Centre. Crafts and Crumbs members are working on embroidered pictures, knitted Christmas baubles and crochet throws.
Our next members’ meeting is scheduled for 2.00pm on Wednesday 18th November (Christmas crafts), subject to a new committee being in place following the AGM.

articles.title: Shepley Naturalists’ Society: The year turns
articles.author: Graham Bennett & Rodger Schofield
articles.summary: A stroll around Wentworth Castle and the first winter walk at Dale Dyke Reservoir.
body: For the last outing of the summer season, a group of eight tackled the grounds of Wentworth Castle. Deer were spotted lazing under trees and there was a good display of autumn crocus. Four intrepid members climbed Stainborough Castle tower.
Dale Dyke Reservoir – the first of our monthly winter walks. Fly agaric and blushing wood mushrooms, buzzards soaring overhead and inquisitive goats on the way back.
Website: shepley-naturalists.weebly.com

articles.title: Shepley Methodist Church: Is something missing?
articles.author: Kimm
articles.summary: Friendship and belonging, the Oasis café, November preaching rota and Harvest raising over £500 for WaterAid.
body: People seem to be losing the confidence and ability to form relationships. If you’re wondering if there’s something missing in life, pop into our Oasis café on Monday or Friday afternoons, 1:30–3:30. Sunday services 10:45–11:45; Bible study on the last Sunday of the month 9:30–10:30.

Preaching rota: 1 Nov Rev Sue Pegg (Holy Communion); 8 Nov Rev Sue Pegg (Village Remembrance Service); 15 Nov Laura Tunnicliffe; 22 Nov Elaine Nixon; 29 Nov Beth Crehan, with Bible Study led by Kimm Brook.
Harvest: generous donations of food went to the Methodist Welcome Centre, and the homemade soup lunch and apple puddings raised over £500 for WaterAid.

articles.title: St Paul’s Church: Remembering
articles.author: Rev Lindsey Barber
articles.summary: November, the season of remembering – a hand-made poppy, All Souls, and the services for November.
body: November is the season of remembering. Armistice Day falls within the Church’s season of remembering, after All Saints (1st November) and All Souls (2nd November).

About five years ago my daughter gifted me a hand-made poppy – number 167 of 454, made for each British service person who lost their life in the Afghan War. I wear it to remember Private Robert McLaren of The Black Watch.

Services: Contemplative Space Tuesdays 10–12; Holy Communion Wednesdays 10am. 1 Nov 5pm Contemplative Communion; 2 Nov 7pm All Souls; 8 Nov 10.45am Remembrance at the Methodist Church; 15 Nov 11.15am Holy Communion & 5pm Contemplative Service; 22 Nov 11.15am; 29 Nov 4pm Advent Hope Reflection at St John Upper Denby.

articles.title: Shepley Library: Our new Huddersfield Library is open
articles.author: We Are: Shepley Library
articles.summary: Free Kirklees membership and eBooks, a WW2 story on 26 November, launch events at the new Huddersfield Library Hub, and regular sessions.
body: Join Kirklees Libraries online for instant access to 30,000 eBooks, eAudio books, newspapers and magazines. Membership, eBooks and reservations are all free – and there are no overdue fines.
Nigel Proud joins us for an emotional retelling of his grandfather’s experiences in World War 2 – Thursday 26th November, 10.30am. No need to book.

Launch events continue at the new Huddersfield Library Hub with Arts Council England – authors, illustrators, performance and makerspace events. Regular: Rhyme Time Mondays 2.30pm; Lego & Duplo Club Fri 2–5 and Sat 10–12; Coffee & Conversation last Thursday; Craft Taster 3rd Thursday; Family History one-to-ones last Friday.
Opening hours: Monday 1–5pm, Thursday 10am–5pm (closed 1–2), Friday 2–5pm, Saturday 10am–12noon. Tel 01484 414868.

articles.title: Hear from our advertisers: Zumba with Tricia
articles.author: Tricia
articles.summary: Former Shepley Band conductor Tricia brings feel-good dance fitness to St Paul’s Church Hall on Thursday mornings.
body: I conducted Shepley Band for many years. Two years ago a free “try before you buy” month at the leisure centre introduced me to dance fitness – Zumba in particular – and it was an utter revelation.

What I’ve started in Shepley is a chance to share some feel-good dance vibes in the church hall next to St Paul’s. If enough folk are interested I’ll introduce chair-based Zumba and Chi Chi Fit. Come and join me on Thursday morning!

articles.title: Reflections on… My time as an Evacuee in Shepley (Part 1)
articles.author: Angela Sexton (née Stiff)
articles.summary: Sent from London to Smithy Hill in 1942: life with Mr and Mrs Dransfield, the fields off Jos Lane and wartime school dinners.
body: I was born in Fulham in 1938. In February 1942 I moved to Smithy Hill, Shepley, to live with Mr and Mrs Dransfield. Mr Dransfield had been deafened in the World War One trenches and worked as a night foreman in the woollen mill. Mrs Dransfield made all my clothes from recycled material.
I spent a great deal of time in the fields off Jos Lane, picking wildflowers and blackberries, and went down Stone Wood Lane to the stream to ‘fish’ for tiddlers. The Rec had a seesaw and swings.

At the local school we had dinner at long trestle tables. My favourite was rice pudding, and if you had been good you were given the container to scrape out. We practised our letters in trays of sand. To be continued.

articles.title: Friends of Shepley First School: Christmas Fair, Friday 27th November
articles.author: Gillian & Team FOSFS
articles.summary: Summer Fair raised £691.87; Santa’s grotto returns at the Christmas Fair, with a raffle and a call for helpers.
body: A HUGE thank you to everyone who supported our Summer Fair – we raised a fantastic £691.87!

Our Christmas Fair is on Friday 27th November and Santa has confirmed he’ll be joining us in his grotto again. We’ll need extra pairs of hands to set up and clear away, and local businesses are invited to donate raffle prizes.
Contact the school office on 01484 603230 or office@shepleyfirst.org.

articles.title: Shepley Village Association: Meeting held on 13th October
articles.author: Jim Reid
articles.summary: Station benches installed, bulb planting on 14 November, Remembrance arrangements and the next meeting on 10 November.
body: Friends of Shepley Station: the benches have been installed and commemorative plaques are in progress.

Bulb planting is planned for Saturday 14th November 2026 – meet at the library 10:30am. Planning for next year’s May Day event is starting. Help is wanted from someone with a petrol strimmer for the War Memorial garden and library area.
Remembrance Sunday service at the Methodist Church at 10:45am, plus a service at the Memorial on 11th November. Next meeting: Tuesday 10th November, 7:30pm in the library.

articles.title: Shepley Fields Forever
articles.author: Shepley Fields Forever
articles.summary: A proposed planning application off Penistone Road in Shelley, and the new national planning delegation scheme.
body: There is now a proposed planning application for fields off Penistone Road in Shelley. We are in contact with the new Shelley steering committee to offer support.
The National Scheme of Delegation of Planning Functions comes into force at the end of October. Please keep your comments coming to D.C.Admin@kirklees.gov.uk.

articles.title: Honouring the heroes of Shepley: Remembrance Sunday at the War Memorial
articles.author: Dinah
articles.summary: The Last Post, wreaths and a minute’s silence at Shepley War Memorial.
body: At 11am on the 8th of November at Shepley War Memorial “The Last Post” will acknowledge the ultimate sacrifice paid by all the fallen in World Wars I and II. We will lay wreaths, commemorative poems will be read and a minute’s silence will be observed.

articles.title: Letter from our Member of Parliament: Working on issues raised by residents
articles.author: Jade Botterill MP
articles.summary: Penistone Road crossing repairs at Far Bank, power cuts and Northern Powergrid, and support for local micro-businesses.
body: In Shelley, the Penistone Road at the bottom of Far Bank will now be included in the council’s upcoming programme of repair works, following concerns raised at my coffee morning.

I have been working with residents, Northern Powergrid and GTC to address frequent power cuts. Northern Powergrid believe they have identified the main fault; please keep reaching out so I know where they need to deliver more.
Contact: jade.botterill.mp@parliament.uk

articles.title: Councillor’s letter: Apologies
articles.author: Shepley Magazine
articles.summary: Cllr John Taylor is unwell this month – who to contact in his absence.
body: John Taylor, our Kirklees Councillor, is currently unwell and unable to write his regular report. We all wish him a speedy recovery.
In John’s absence please contact Cllr Richard Smith (richard.smith@kirklees.gov.uk) or Cllr Bill Armer (bill.armer@kirklees.gov.uk).

articles.title: Woodley School: Giants visit Woodley!
articles.author: Woodley School & College
articles.summary: Prize-winning giant vegetables from the Harrogate Autumn Flower Show inspire pupils’ horticulture skills.
body: Giant vegetables from the Harrogate Autumn Flower Show visited Woodley School & College, a specialist school for pupils with autism in Huddersfield, courtesy of Paula Haley of the Professional Gardener’s Guild.

Two of the vegetables weighed over 25kg. Pupils harvested seeds to grow their own next year, and the visit opened up conversations about farming, horticulture and greengrocery as careers. Local businesses who could offer work encounters are invited to contact Claire Thompson at the school.

articles.title: Shepley Health Centre: Drop-in Wellness Service at Shepley Library
articles.author: Shepley Health Centre
articles.summary: Kirklees Wellness Service drop-ins, The Mast Integrated Neighbourhood Team, and flu & COVID vaccinations.
body: The Kirklees Wellness Service helps you become more active, improve your diet, manage your weight or stop smoking. Drop-in at Shepley Library on Mondays 3:00–4:45pm, or visit kirkleeswellnessservice.co.uk.
The Mast primary care network serves over 35,000 patients. Its Integrated Neighbourhood Team was chosen as the first accelerator site in Kirklees, focusing on support after hospital discharge.
Flu & COVID vaccinations 2026 – have you booked yours yet? We have availability for all eligible patients.

articles.title: A snapshot of Shepley’s history: Lydgate Road
articles.author: Clare Francis
articles.summary: “Lidgit”: Joshua Wood’s shop and bakehouse, the 1879 fire, Lydgate House, Pinfold Cottage and the greengrocer’s pony and cart.
body: Pronounced ‘Lidgit’, this road did originally have a gate on it. At the top, where it meets Station Road, was a grocers, confectioners and corn merchants run by Joshua Wood. In December 1879 an overheating chimney flue set fire to cloth goods – £100 of stock was destroyed.

Lydgate House was a laith house with weaver’s windows, later occupied by merchant tailor Walter Wortley. Pinfold Cottage stood near the pinfold, where stray animals were penned. Until about the 1950s greengrocer George Henry Heeley sold produce round the village by pony and cart.

articles.title: Shepley Bird and Wildlife Group: A love for the wild & our duty to protect it
articles.author: Cathy Evans
articles.summary: PC Caroline Newsome on wildlife crime, a badger stuck on a roof, and next month’s ‘Tales From a River Bank’.
body: Our October talk was given by PC Caroline Newsome, Kirklees Wildlife, Rural and Heritage Crime Officer, who fosters hedgehogs and keeps eight disabled hedgehogs safe in her garden. Wildlife crime is hard to investigate – there are rarely witnesses and the animals cannot tell their stories.
The most endearing incident: a badger stuck on a roof, rescued by a two-pronged team – at the cost of one badger bite!
Next indoor meeting: Wednesday 4th November, 7.30pm, Coach House, Cliffe House – Mick Forster Jones, ‘Tales From a River Bank’. Visitors £3; membership £15 a year. shepleybirders@yahoo.com

articles.title: Cliffe House: A celebration of creativity and community
articles.author: Nigel Hoyle & the Art at the House team
articles.summary: Art at the House welcomed over 2,000 visitors, a new stone monolith sculpture and a real piano in the woods.
body: Art at the House took place at Cliffe House on 19th and 20th September. With funding from Kirklees Seasons of Culture and Kirkburton Parish Council we expanded onto the front lawn and grew the woodland market.

A stone monolith sculpture by Ryan James was installed and will be finished with your help over the next couple of years. Well over 2,000 people came for workshops, live music and quality art and crafts. artatthehouse.co.uk

articles.title: Cliffe House Christmas Fayre and Market
articles.author: Friends of Cliffe House
articles.summary: Stalls, Scissett Youth Band, food from Rations of Skelmanthorpe and Santa’s sleigh – Saturday 28 November.
body: Start the festive season at Cliffe House: an eclectic mix of stalls, live music from Scissett Youth Band, food from Rations of Skelmanthorpe, snowman-making for children, and Santa arriving on his sleigh before heading to his Grotto. Saturday 28th November, 11am–3pm.

articles.title: Readers’ letters
articles.author: Readers
articles.summary: Poppies in St Paul’s graveyard, and £500 raised at an Evening of Fashion with Queen Bea’s.
body: Poppies in St Paul’s Church graveyard: walking around, I felt quite emotional noticing the number of graves marked with poppies, illustrating how many Shepley families have been affected by war.

Many thanks to Natalie at Queen Bea’s boutique for the fashion show on 9th October in St Paul’s Church. Ticket sales and the Vintage rail raised £500 towards a replacement church boiler. – Judith Parkes

articles.title: Shepley’s snippets: readers’ photographs
articles.author: Readers
articles.summary: Rainbows, autumn sunsets, deer in Shepley fields, geese flying west and a young snail with a passenger.
body: This month’s gallery from readers Pete, Angela, Carol, Paul, Lucy, Pauline, Catherine, Allan and Dave: the end of the rainbow, a beautiful sky, a horse in Hepworth, great tits nesting in a bird box, Stones Wood, deer in Shepley fields, sunset over Lea Drive, geese flying westwards over Shepley and a young snail with a passenger.

articles.title: Shepley Cricket Club Bonfire & Firework Display – Thursday 5th November
articles.author: Matthew Hartley, Chairman
articles.summary: E-tickets via QR code, please walk if you can, food, bars and fireworks by Pyro 2000. Gates 5pm, bonfire 6pm, fireworks 7.30pm.
body: Shepley Cricket Club will once again host its annual Bonfire & Firework Display on Thursday 5th November. Electronic ticketing continues – scan the QR code to buy tickets. £7 adult, £5 child, £20 family (2 adults & 2 children). Gates open 5pm, bonfire lit 6pm, fireworks 7:30pm.
The club is not permitted to manage traffic or parking on the public highway. Please walk to the club if possible; if you must drive, park considerately.
Full bar, can and prosecco bars, doughnuts, chilli, hotdogs, pie & peas, vegetarian curry and parkin, “Milk on the Hills”, fireworks by Pyro 2000 Ltd, supported by St John Ambulance.

articles.title: Emley AFC: Forthcoming fixtures
articles.author: Emley AFC
articles.summary: Home to Whitby Town on 7 November and Hyde United on 21 November.
body: Saturday 7th November, 3:00pm – Whitby Town. Saturday 21st November, 3:00pm – Hyde United. Saturday gates open 1pm. Fixtures subject to change – check emleyafc.co.uk.

articles.title: Shepley Cricket Club: Bringing the season to a close
articles.author: Matthew Hartley, Chairman
articles.summary: Senior Presentation Night awards, the league-winning Under-9s and work starting on the Nursery Ground.
body: Our Senior Presentation Night celebrated another season. Awards included Connor Dale (1st XI Players’ Player and Captain’s Player of the Year), James Tate and Teddy Hartley (2nd XI), the Trevor Curtis Trophy (Alison Rose) and Junior Clubman of the Year (Kitty Dawson), alongside our Huddersfield League-winning Under-9s.
Renovation of the square is underway for 2027, and diggers are on site for the long-awaited Nursery Ground project.
